content_units: California Freelancer Setup at a Glance
For a freelance graphic designer in California earning about   $85,000/year   with   low overhead   and   no employees  , the biggest trade-offs are:
-   Liability protection:   LLC is stronger
-   Cost and paperwork:   sole proprietorship is simpler and cheaper
-   Taxes:   often similar at this income level unless special tax elections are used
-   California-specific cost:   LLCs have a meaningful annual state cost that sole props avoid
LLC vs Sole Proprietorship for a California Graphic Designer
Factor   Sole Proprietorship   LLC (single-member, default tax treatment)   Practical takeaway
Legal status   No separate legal entity; you and the business are the same   Separate legal entity under California law   LLC is better if you want a cleaner legal separation

Personal liability     No liability shield   for business debts, contract disputes, some client claims     Limited liability protection   for many business obligations if properly maintained   LLC is usually better if liability is a serious concern
Startup cost in California   Very low; usually just local license/DBA if needed   Formation filing plus ongoing CA requirements   Sole prop is cheaper and easier to start

Ongoing California cost   Minimal in many cases   California LLCs generally face the   $800 annual franchise tax   and may owe an additional LLC fee at higher gross receipts   For $85k revenue, the LLC cost is a major deciding factor

Federal income tax   Profit usually reported on   Schedule C     By default, single-member LLC usually also reports on   Schedule C     For many freelancers, baseline federal tax filing is very similar
Self-employment tax   Yes, generally applies to net business profit   Yes, generally applies by default to net business profit   Default LLC does   not   automatically reduce self-employment tax
California income tax   Passed through to owner   Passed through to owner by default   Similar in many one-owner cases
Business bank/account separation   Recommended but not legally distinct   Strongly recommended to preserve liability shield   LLC needs cleaner separation to work properly
Paperwork and admin   Lowest burden   More filings, recordkeeping, and compliance   Sole prop wins on simplicity
Credibility with clients   Usually acceptable for freelancers   Can look more formal in contracts/invoices   LLC may help with presentation, but usually not essential

Best fit for your profile   Good if you want low cost and simple operations   Good if client-risk exposure matters more than added cost/admin   Your choice mainly turns on liability concern vs California LLC cost
When Each Option Usually Makes Sense
Option 1: Sole Proprietorship   Lowest cost and least paperwork   Best for simplicity
- You have   low business risk
- You mainly do design deliverables, not products, events, or large subcontracted projects
- You want to keep admin minimal
- You are comfortable relying heavily on   good contracts   and   business insurance
- The added California LLC cost feels too high for your current stage
Option 2: Single-Member LLC   Better liability structure   Best for risk separation
- You sign larger client contracts or worry about disputes, indemnity clauses, or missed-deadline claims
- You want a clearer wall between   business obligations   and   personal assets
- You plan to grow, hire, take retainers, or work with bigger brands/agencies
- You are willing to pay California’s annual LLC cost for that structure
- You will actually maintain the LLC correctly: separate finances, contracts in LLC name, required filings
Practical Decision Checklist
Choose   sole proprietorship   if most of these are true:
- You want the   lowest-cost   setup now
- Your work is mostly straightforward freelance design services
- You have no employees and limited legal exposure
- You can protect yourself with a strong client agreement, clear scope terms, and professional liability insurance
- You may revisit an LLC later if revenue or risk increases
Choose   LLC   if most of these are true:
- Your top priority is   liability protection
- You work with clients where disputes, chargebacks, IP issues, or contract claims are realistic concerns
- You want a more formal business structure before scaling
- You are fine with extra filings and California annual costs
- You will keep business operations separate enough to support the liability shield
Best Fit for Your Situation
Given   $85,000 revenue  ,   low equipment costs  ,   no employees  , and concern about   liability, taxes, and paperwork  :
- If your strongest concern is   simplicity and minimizing cost  , a   sole proprietorship   is usually the more practical choice right now.

- If your strongest concern is   liability protection  , a   single-member LLC   is usually the better choice, even though the tax benefit may be limited at this stage and the California annual cost is significant.
- For many California solo creatives at this size, the real comparison is:
-   Sole prop + solid contract + insurance   vs
-   LLC + higher annual state cost + more admin
A common practical view: at your revenue level, an LLC is often chosen more for   risk management and professionalism   than for basic tax savings.
